reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: This is a cardiac contractility modulation (CCM) device trial, not a drug trial. The OPTIMIZER System delivers electrical stimulation to improve cardiac contractility. No biomarker data is available to assess target engagement, but the device was implanted and presumably delivered electrical stimulation as intended. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No biomarker data is available to assess whether the electrical stimulation actually improved myocardial contractility or cardiac output as proposed. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint of exercise tolerance (VAT) failed - 38/210 responders in treatment vs 28/212 in control (p=0.31). The composite safety endpoint also failed (112/210 vs 103/212 events, p=0.125). 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial appears adequately powered (n=428) and of sufficient duration (50 weeks). There were some safety concerns including higher sepsis rates (4.8% vs 0.9%) and device-related complications, but these don't appear to have limited dosing since this is a device trial with fixed stimulation parameters.

failure_modes.evidence: No biomarker data available to assess target engagement or pathway modulation. Cannot determine where in the causal chain the failure occurred - whether the device failed to engage cardiac contractility, whether contractility improved but didn't translate to exercise tolerance, or other factors.
